target_customer: Career changers and aspiring developers paying tuition, later universities and employers partnering for bootcamps
problem: Software engineering skills were hard to learn quickly, and a JavaScript focused immersive program offered a faster route to a developer job.
business_model: Tuition based coding bootcamp, with deferred tuition options and later university partnerships

founders.name: Nimit Maru
founders.background_notes: YC page: senior software engineer at Yahoo Maps and Travel; later founded Sava. Education from Illinois ECE article.

founders.name: David Yang
founders.background_notes: Co-founder per Illinois ECE article and YC page; no bio on the YC page.

exit.reason: Zovio bought all outstanding shares; total purchase price per its 10-K. Zovio later dissolved and sold Fullstack to Simplilearn in Nov 2022 for an undisclosed all cash price.

competitors.name: Hack Reactor
competitors.what: San Francisco 12 week software engineering bootcamp founded 2012

technical_complexity.rationale: A school, not a technology product; the hard parts were curriculum, instructors and hiring outcomes.

defensibility.rationale: Reputation and employer relationships helped, but bootcamps copy each other easily and compete on placement and price.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competing bootcamps multiplied; Fullstack was bought by Zovio in 2019 for about 33 million dollars.

market_need_then: Demand for developers was high in 2012 and a wave of bootcamps launched that year; the school began enrolling in 2013 per Wikipedia and graduated over 2,500 students by 2019 per the Illinois ECE article.

branding.domain_note: Uses fullstackacademy.com, the exact .com for the Academy suffix name.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct career change pitch (bootcamps prepare you to succeed in tech)

branding.brand_signature: Grace Hopper Program, a program for women and non-binary students launched in 2016
branding.community_and_virality: The Grace Hopper Program and a New York City fellowship drew press; alumni reviews on bootcamp sites. No merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Well known among bootcamps with university partnerships and a distinctive women focused program, but the name is a generic tech term.

outcome_analysis: Fullstack opened its New York bootcamp in 2013 with little disclosed outside capital, grew to over 2,500 graduates and university partnerships, and was acquired by Zovio on 2019-04-01 for a reported total purchase price of about 33 million dollars. Founders left in 2021, Zovio dissolved and Simplilearn bought it in Nov 2022, so the business survived under new owners.
notes: Price conflict: Illinois ECE (Apr 2019) says 17.5M cash plus 2.5M shares; Zovio 10-K (via a search summary of its filings) puts total consideration at 33.3M including 17.7M cash, 12.3M equity, 3.25M contingent. SEC figures taken from search summary, not opened. Search summaries also say founders took 25K to 50K angel checks and were otherwise bootstrapped, and that they left in mid 2021; not read in an opened source so no rounds recorded. YC page lists Summer 2012, Wikipedia says Spring 2012. Competitor sources are generic and not dated precisely; coding bootcamps launched in 2012 per a Wikipedia entry. Company site fullstackacademy.com fetched and shows live online bootcamps with no ownership text.
